findings.description: The RDS instance has storage_encrypted set to false, so the catalog database is stored unencrypted on disk and in snapshots.
publicly_accessible is true, giving the MySQL database a publicly resolvable address reachable from outside the VPC.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database password (var.password) in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, where it is readable from the instance and stored in instance metadata and launch config, exposing the DB credential.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the instance role full control over storage, compute and databases including the ability to modify policies and assume downstream roles.

The application instance runs Apache and is attached to portal_sg and a public subnet; combined with the wildcard IAM role and embedded DB credentials, compromise of this internet-facing host yields full account access.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports and protocols, permitting unrestricted data exfiltration if the DB host is compromised.

backup_retention_period is 0 and skip_final_snapshot is true, so no automated or final snapshots exist; this is an operational/reliability concern rather than a security vulnerability and is noted only for completeness.
